facts.raw_span: a small lump in his right hemiscrotum two months earlier during self-examination
no prior medical history
denied any history of scrotal trauma or inflammation
the lump’s size remained unchanged over two months
only mild discomfort during exercise, which resolved with rest
a painless, round, hazelnut-sized mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis
the testicles and groin were otherwise unremarkable
Scrotal ultrasonography demonstrated a solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused 1.3 × 1.1 cm mass at the tail of the right epididymis
containing two small hypoechoic foci, with no invasion of adjacent structures
Routine blood tests, coagulation profile, and serum tumor markers (AFP, LDH, CEA, and β-HCG) were all within normal limits

concepts.why: The presence of a painless, round, hazelnut-sized mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis, as well as the ultrasonography findings of a solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused mass with two small hypoechoic foci, are consistent with an epididymal cyst.
The presence of a mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis could be consistent with epididymitis, although the lack of reported inflammation or trauma makes this diagnosis less likely.

The ultrasonography findings of a solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused mass with two small hypoechoic foci are consistent with an adenomatoid tumor of the epididymis, a rare benign tumor.
The presence of a painless, round, hazelnut-sized mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis could be consistent with a lipoma of the epididymis, a rare benign tumor.

The presence of a mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis could be consistent with epididymal sarcoidosis, although this diagnosis would typically be associated with systemic symptoms and other findings.

rationales.F08: Scrotal ultrasonography demonstrating a solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused mass is highly suggestive of epididymal cyst or adenomatoid tumor.
